lessons.title: Feel ready for your first race
lessons.description: Know where to go, what to listen for and how to learn from every swim.

steps.title: Prepare before you arrive
steps.text: Good preparation starts the night before, not when you are called to race.
bullets: Read which races you are entered in and check the meet arrangements. Pack your race kit, caps, goggles, spare kit, extra towels, poolside clothing, drinks and food. Plan your meals and arrival time, and get a good night’s rest.
Eat your planned pre-meet meal, check that your kit and extra towels are packed, and bring the food and drinks you will need. Arrive prepared, knowing which races you are swimming.

steps.title: Stay with your team and listen
steps.text: Your team managers are responsible for you on poolside and in the pool hall. Stay with the team, stay engaged and listen. Do not wander off to see your parents. You must be where the team managers can reach you; they will not come looking for you. If you need to leave the team area, speak to a team manager first.
bullets: Your team manager will tell you when to go to marshalling, where swimmers gather before racing. That does not replace your responsibility to listen and be ready. Go promptly when directed, listen for your name or heat, and ask if you are unsure.

steps.title: Arrive at your lane ready to race
steps.text: Know your race, heat and lane, and understand the plan you have discussed with your coach. Have your equipment ready. Put your cap and goggles on before you reach your lane so you arrive ready to race.
bullets: Your cap and goggles should already be on. Take off your outer clothing, keeping your swimming costume on, and get ready. If needed, you can dry the block down, especially if it has no wedge. Do this before the start procedure and follow the officials’ directions.

steps.title: The whistle is not the starting signal
steps.text: For a dive start, short whistles mean get ready and the long whistle means get onto the block. Take your starting position on “take your marks”. Only the starting signal starts the race.

steps.title: Backstroke has two long whistles
steps.text: Enter the water on the first long whistle. Return to the starting position on the second. Face the starting end and hold the grips with both hands. Wait for the command and then the starting signal.

steps.title: Keep racing, then learn
steps.text: If your goggles come off, keep swimming and complete the race without touching or trying to fix them. Afterwards, return to your coach for feedback. A DQ is disappointing, but it is a chance to understand one thing and practise it for next time.

lessons.takeaway: Prepare before you arrive, stay with your team, listen for instructions and go to your lane ready to race. Afterwards, take one useful piece of feedback back to training.

lessons.title: Make sense of the start
lessons.description: Practise the signals and positions for dive and water starts.

steps.title: Dive start: wait, position, go
steps.text: Get onto the platform on the long whistle. On “take your marks”, take your starting position with at least one foot touching the front. The rule does not prescribe a position for your hands. Be still and wait for the starting signal.

steps.title: Water start: face the starting end
steps.text: Backstroke and medley relay start in the water. Hold the starting grips with both hands. When using a backstroke ledge, at least one toe of each foot contacts the wall or touchpad; do not bend toes over its top. Do not stand in or on the gutter, or bend your toes over its lip.

steps.title: If the start is reset
steps.text: Do not guess or dive. Listen to the officials. If an early-start disqualification is declared before the signal, the procedure repeats from the appropriate long whistle. For backstroke, return to the starting position.

lessons.takeaway: Whistles prepare the race; the starting signal begins it. Follow the official if a start is reset.

lessons.title: Freestyle: wall to wall
lessons.description: Understand breakout, wall contact and the finish exception.

steps.title: Start and swimming
steps.text: A freestyle-only race permits any swimming style; front crawl is commonly used. After the start and every turn, your head must break the surface at or before 15m. A breakout at 15.01m is late.

steps.title: Turning: make contact
steps.text: Some part of your body must touch the wall at the end of every length. In a tumble turn, feet can make that contact. Being close to the wall is not enough.

steps.title: Finishing: a specific exception
steps.text: Normally, some part of your body remains at the surface. Once your head has passed the final 5m marker, complete submersion is allowed when reaching for the finish wall. This does not allow swimming the whole final 5m underwater or apply to an ordinary turn.

lessons.takeaway: Head up by 15m. Touch every wall. Keep the finish exception separate from a turn.

lessons.title: Backstroke: know which wall action you need
lessons.description: Separate ordinary swimming, a turn and the final touch.

steps.title: Start and swimming
steps.text: Start in the water, facing the starting end and holding the grips. Push away on your back. During ordinary swimming you may roll towards either side, but less than 90 degrees from horizontal; head position does not decide body orientation.

steps.title: Break out by 15 metres
steps.text: Your head must have broken the surface at or before 15m after the start and each turn. A hand breaking the surface earlier does not replace that requirement.

steps.title: A turn has its own sequence
steps.text: For a backstroke-to-backstroke turn, you may rotate beyond vertical towards your front. Any arm action used to initiate the turn must be an immediate continuous single-arm pull or simultaneous double-arm pull. Touch the wall with some part of your body and leave on your back.

steps.title: A finish is not that turn
steps.text: At the finish, touch while still on your back. This also applies when finishing the backstroke leg of an individual medley. There is a finish-reaching submersion allowance after the head passes the final 5m marker.

lessons.takeaway: Leave a backstroke turn on your back; finish the backstroke leg with a touch on your back.

lessons.title: Breaststroke: pullout, rhythm and touch
lessons.description: Learn the pullout limit, simultaneous actions and the two-hand wall contact.

steps.title: The pullout after a start or turn
steps.text: One underwater arm pull may go back to the legs. One optional butterfly kick is allowed before the first breaststroke kick. Your head must have broken the surface before the hands turn inward at the widest part of the second arm stroke. Surfacing earlier is allowed. This is not a 15m test.

steps.title: Swimming together
steps.text: Arms act together; legs act together. Turn your feet outwards in the propulsive kick. During every complete stroke cycle, some part of your head breaks the surface. The ordinary rhythm is one pull followed by one kick.

steps.title: Two hands at every turn and finish
steps.text: Touch with both hands simultaneously, without stacking them. They may touch at different heights; incidental finger contact is allowed. The final arm stroke into a turn or finish may omit its following kick. The head may be submerged after the last pull, provided it broke the surface during the last complete or incomplete cycle before the touch.

steps.title: Turn departure: read the later clarification
steps.text: World Aquatics’ August guidance requires rotation past vertical towards the breast before any kick after a turn, including the optional dolphin kick, as well as breast orientation before the first arm pull. This app still flags the England application for confirmation. This point is explained here but is not used to score your answers.

lessons.takeaway: Move together, know the pullout surfacing test, and bring two hands to the wall together.

lessons.title: Butterfly: together through the race
lessons.description: Connect simultaneous actions, breakout and the touch.

steps.title: Swimming: arms and legs together
steps.text: Recover both arms forward together over the water and pull them back together underwater. Move the legs up and down together; different heights are allowed, alternating movements are not. A breaststroke kick is not allowed.

steps.title: Start and underwater phase
steps.text: After a start or turn, the underwater allowance includes one or more kicks and one arm pull that brings you to the surface. The head must break the surface at or before 15m.

steps.title: Turn and finish touches
steps.text: Touch with both hands simultaneously, without stacking them. Different heights and incidental finger contact are allowed. When reaching for the finish wall, complete submersion is allowed after the head passes the final 5m marker.

steps.title: Turn departure differs from breaststroke
steps.text: The August World Aquatics clarification requires the body to be on the breast after leaving the wall. Do not use the breaststroke turn permission as a butterfly technique. England application remains flagged in this app, so this departure point is not scored.

lessons.takeaway: Move together, break out by 15m and touch with two hands together.

lessons.title: Medley and relays: get the change right
lessons.description: Practise stroke order, stroke changes and team takeovers.

steps.title: Two races, two orders
steps.text: Individual medley: butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, freestyle. Medley relay: backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, freestyle. In medley freestyle, do not use backstroke, breaststroke or butterfly.

steps.title: Medley freestyle: turn first, then kick
steps.text: In medley freestyle, the body must be on the breast except during a turn. You may leave a turn on your back, but must rotate past vertical towards the breast before any kick or stroke. This includes a dolphin kick. This is the medley freestyle rule, separate from the flagged breaststroke departure guidance.

steps.title: Finish one stroke before starting the next
steps.text: Each medley section ends using that stroke’s finish rule. For backstroke to breaststroke, touch while on your back before turning. Do not apply the backstroke tumble-turn permission to the end of the backstroke section.

steps.title: The relay takeover
steps.text: Your feet must keep contact with the starting platform until the incoming swimmer touches the wall. The key moment is feet leaving, not the start of preparatory body movement.

steps.title: Clear the water considerately
steps.text: After an individual race, wait until all competitors finish and follow officials’ directions. With over-the-top starts, stay tight to the wall and lane rope, then leave promptly after the next race starts. After a relay leg, leave promptly without obstruction unless you are the last team swimmer; then wait as for an individual race.

lessons.takeaway: Know which order you are swimming, finish each stroke legally and watch the incoming touch.

lessons.title: Look closer: small details matter
lessons.description: Compare clear examples and learn which detail changes the answer.

steps.title: Breakout: the head must surface by 15m
steps.text: For freestyle, backstroke and butterfly, the head must have broken the surface at or before 15m after a start or turn. Look at the head and the distance together. A hand surfacing earlier does not meet this requirement.

examples.label: Meets the breakout deadline
examples.text: The head first breaks the surface at exactly 15m.

examples.label: Misses the breakout deadline
examples.text: A hand surfaces at 14m, but the head first surfaces at 15.01m.

steps.title: Two-hand touch: together does not mean level
steps.text: For breaststroke and butterfly, both hands must touch at the same time and must not be stacked. Equal height and a visible gap are not extra requirements. Assess the touch described, not whether it looks unusual.

examples.label: Meets the touch requirement
examples.text: Both hands touch simultaneously at different heights, without being stacked.

examples.label: Does not meet the touch requirement
examples.text: One hand touches first and the other arrives a moment later.

steps.title: Finish allowance: it does not apply at a turn
steps.text: In freestyle, complete submersion is allowed after the head has passed the final 5m marker when reaching for the finish wall. This is a specific finish allowance, not permission to swim an entire final 5m underwater or to submerge early on the approach to an ordinary turn.

examples.label: The finish allowance applies
examples.text: In the final length, the head has passed the 5m marker. The swimmer becomes fully submerged while reaching for the finish wall.

examples.label: The finish allowance does not apply
examples.text: With more lengths still to swim, the swimmer becomes fully submerged 4m before the wall while still approaching it, before beginning the turn. The finish allowance cannot justify this.

steps.title: Relay takeover: watch the feet, not the arms
steps.text: An outgoing relay swimmer may begin preparatory movement before the incoming swimmer touches. The feet must keep contact with the platform until that touch. Starting an arm swing and leaving the block are different events.

examples.label: Meets the takeover contact requirement
examples.text: The arms swing before the incoming touch, but the feet stay on the block until the touch.

examples.label: Does not meet the takeover contact requirement
examples.text: The feet leave before the incoming touch, even though the swimmer enters the water afterwards.

steps.title: Three other details to carry forward
steps.text: Bring the earlier lessons together: check the whole sequence, not just the final position.
bullets: Backstroke turn: an immediate continuous single-arm or simultaneous double-arm pull may initiate the turn. Make wall contact and leave on your back.

Breaststroke pullout: at most one butterfly kick before the first breaststroke kick; the head must surface before the hands turn inward at the widest part of the second arm stroke. Earlier surfacing is allowed.
Medley change: finish the outgoing stroke legally. In the freestyle section, rotate from a back departure past vertical towards the breast before any kick or stroke.

lessons.takeaway: Name the stroke, the phase and the exact timing before making the call.

startCoaching: For our dive start, put your hands over the front edge of the block. Your thumbs and palms should not rest on the top of the block. The aim is to push back against the block with your hands at the start. Practise this position with your coach. This is club technique advice; the rule does not prescribe a hand position.

meetPreparation.title: The night before
meetPreparation.text: Read which races you are entered in and check the meet arrangements. Pack your race kit, caps, goggles, spare kit, extra towels, poolside clothing, drinks and food. Plan your meals and arrival time, and get a good night’s rest.

meetPreparation.title: Before you leave home
meetPreparation.text: Eat your planned pre-meet meal, check that your kit and extra towels are packed, and bring the food and drinks you will need. Arrive prepared, knowing which races you are swimming.

meetPreparation.title: Stay with your team
meetPreparation.text: Your team managers are responsible for you on poolside and in the pool hall. Stay with the team, stay engaged and listen. Do not wander off to see your parents. You must be where the team managers can reach you; they will not come looking for you. If you need to leave the team area, speak to a team manager first.

meetPreparation.title: When it is time for marshalling
meetPreparation.text: Your team manager will tell you when to go to marshalling, where swimmers gather before racing. That does not replace your responsibility to listen and be ready. Go promptly when directed, listen for your name or heat, and ask if you are unsure.

meetPreparation.title: Before you go to your lane
meetPreparation.text: Know your race, heat and lane, and understand the plan you have discussed with your coach. Have your equipment ready. Put your cap and goggles on before you reach your lane so you arrive ready to race.

meetPreparation.title: At your lane
meetPreparation.text: Your cap and goggles should already be on. Take off your outer clothing, keeping your swimming costume on, and get ready. If needed, you can dry the block down, especially if it has no wedge. Do this before the start procedure and follow the officials’ directions.

terms.definition: Happening at the same time. At the breaststroke or butterfly wall, both hands must contact at the same instant.
Hands not stacked on top of one another. A visible gap is not required; incidental finger contact is permitted.
The permitted breaststroke sequence after a start or turn, with its one long arm pull, optional single butterfly kick and head-emergence deadline.
Backstroke’s body position allows roll up to, but not including, 90 degrees from horizontal; head position is not decisive.
The change between stroke sections. The outgoing section must first satisfy its own finish rule.
The exchange between swimmers. The outgoing feet retain platform contact until the incoming swimmer touches.
The official with authority over the competition decision, distinct from an observing judge’s report.
One group of swimmers racing at the same time in an event.
Your allocated strip of the pool. Check your heat and lane before going to the start.
The place or process where swimmers are organised before racing. Listen to your team manager and the marshals.
The person supporting and supervising your team on poolside. Stay with the team and tell them before you need to leave the team area.
The raised platform used for a dive start. Get on when instructed by the whistle sequence.
The adjustable inclined foot support at the back of some starting blocks.
A support for the feet at a backstroke start. It does not replace the requirement for at least one toe of each foot to contact the wall or touchpad.
The timing panel on the pool end wall. A swimmer’s contact can trigger the electronic time.
The transition from the underwater phase into swimming at the surface.
One swimmer’s part of a relay race. In a medley, a section also refers to one stroke’s part of the race.
A race combining all four strokes. Individual medley order is butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, freestyle; medley relay order is backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, freestyle.
The side-on boundary between being on the back and being on the breast. Rotation past that boundary towards the front is described as past vertical towards the breast.
Below the water surface. Completely submerged means no part of the body breaks the surface.
Producing the force that moves the swimmer forwards; the propulsive part of the kick is the part that drives the swimmer.
A disqualification means a rule breach affected the result of that swim. Ask your coach what happened and practise the correction; it does not define you as a swimmer.
The next race starts while the previous swimmers wait in the water. Stay tight to the wall and lane rope, follow officials’ instructions, then clear the water promptly after the start.
